newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian trading system equities volume hits record.
newsitem.headline: Russian trading system equities volume hits record.

text.p: Share turnover on the Russian Trading System hit a record volume of $55.01 million on Wednesday, beating a previous high of $46.97 million on October 9, 1996, NAUFOR brokers association data showed.

The Russian Trading System (RTS) 24-share index closed at 227.73, up from 219.86 at close on Monday, the previous day of trade, and just below the record 227.79 set on July 4, 1996 after President Boris Yeltsin's re-election.
The RTS accounts for the bulk of equities trading in Russia.
A number of shares hit new highs in a price rise that traders predicted would continue in the short to medium term but could see a correction.
Mosenergo touched $1.330 and closed at $1.310, after $1.105 on Monday. Irkutskenergo rose to $0.172 from $0.150 and UES firmed to $0.110 from $0.100.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz alone saw 30 million shares change hands and closed at a record $0.60, up from $0.53 on Monday.
"The growth trend will continue for two to three weeks," said Andrei Galperin a trader at Creditanstalt-Grant.
But some dealers said prices had risen too fast since the Christmas holidays began. The RTS index was 189.08 on December 24.
"Our client base is not chasing UES at 11 (cents)," said an analyst at a Western bank who predicted many investors would wait for a correction within the next week or so.
But he said Westerners were responsible for a substantial share of the volume.
